entries.name: VX-94 VSF
entries.summary: Variable-geometry strike fighter built around rapid role conversion and extreme-altitude escape.
entries.detail: Swept fighter geometry favours interception and hypersonic pursuit. Deployed attack geometry exposes the heavy strike bay and broadens surface-fire authority.

entries.name: TWIN CANNON MK I
entries.summary: Synchronized conventional cannon package mounted on registered VX-94 hardpoints.
entries.detail: Low draw and predictable convergence make it the baseline against which experimental stores are evaluated.

entries.name: FIELD COIL MK I
entries.summary: Compact combat dynamo feeding weapons, shielding and tactical systems.
entries.detail: High-output weapons may exceed recovery and temporarily drain the reserve. Fire discipline remains part of loadout design.

entries.name: COMPOSITE FRAME
entries.summary: Carbon-composite primary structure with conventional field emitters.
entries.detail: Later frames add ceramic, reactive and field-coupled layers without changing the VX-94 registered gameplay centre.

entries.name: ATLAS TANKER
entries.summary: Forward tanker and combat rearm aircraft operating at MID and HIGH altitude.
entries.detail: The VX-94 must hold the drogue corridor long enough to transfer energy, bombs and limited support stores.

entries.name: ACE INTERCEPTOR
entries.summary: Aggressive variable-speed hunter flown by Black Flag contract aces.
entries.detail: Unpredictable lateral weave punishes fixed firing lanes. Confirmed examples can sweep their wings and enter hypersonic pursuit.

entries.name: MISSILE CORVETTE
entries.summary: Compact littoral combatant carrying paired missile and deck-gun systems.
entries.detail: Its narrow wake hides substantial armour. Bomber geometry and precision surface stores are recommended.

entries.name: SECURITY PATROL MECH
entries.summary: Human-operated security walker adapted for convoy and facility defence.
entries.detail: Armoured torso and registered weapon articulation make it more dangerous than conventional mobile anti-air units.

entries.name: MACHINE WAR
entries.summary: Autonomous defence systems ceased accepting human command authority.
entries.detail: The first attacks struck both contracted forces. Manufacturing nodes continued operating after every human control link was removed.

entries.name: DRONE HUNTER
entries.summary: Predictive pursuit aircraft optimized to trap repeated movement patterns.
entries.detail: Break rhythm, change altitude and deny a stable lead solution. Some units can enter hypersonic chase geometry.

entries.name: AI FORGE CORE
entries.summary: Self-defending production authority buried inside a converted industrial plant.
entries.detail: Multiple armour and missile phases protect the core. Destroyed peripheral systems alter the final attack cycle.

entries.name: BLACK SKY
entries.summary: Upper-atmosphere campaign against the autonomous strategic network.
entries.detail: The battlespace extends from cloud-top interception to orbital machinery above the planetary rim.

entries.name: PHASE CONTROL ARRAY
entries.summary: Field-control structure coordinating predictive orbital fire lanes.
entries.detail: Emitter loss changes its shield cycle. Fighter geometry is required to exploit the exposed mobile weak point.

entries.name: MACHINE ARK
entries.summary: Final autonomous command vessel and strategic manufacturing authority.
entries.detail: Its layered command shell controls missile broadsides, orbital machinery and the last machine-war production reserve.

entries.name: BLACK WAKE VECTOR
entries.summary: Encrypted pursuit order recovered from a concealed Black Sea interception cell.
entries.detail: The vector proves Black Flag aces were tracking VX-94 altitude transitions before the machine uprising.
